pr.title: Allow more top-down inlining for single-BB callees
pr.description:
This means that things like `<usize as Step>::forward_unchecked` and `<PartialOrd for f32>::le` will inline even if
we've already done a bunch of inlining to find the calls to them.

Fixes #138136

issues.title: MIR inliner, despite running, doesn't always inline trivial things like `i32::le`
issues.body:
IIRC this is due to top-down inlining restrictions, but we should find a way to ensure those restrictions don't apply to things like `<i32 as PartialOrd>::le` which are just a single MIR statement and therefore it's always profitable to inline them, no matter what.

See <https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/138135/files#diff-7f0e93ee8770e4ffe714ae19c6f0f3ab6ae1bc76e3fb03f079e11988fbbab93eR58> for an example.

Alternatively we could consider `InstSimplify`ing them, like we do `clone` calls on primitives.

processing.reason: The PR is an inlining-optimization change, not a value/memory rewrite. Its original and transformed behaviors differ only in whether cheap call sites (e.g. `<usize as Step>::forward_unchecked`, `<f32 as PartialOrd>::le`, Fn shims) are inlined after prior top-down inlining. The old `inline_limit_for_block` restriction and the new depth-aware eligibility both preserve program semantics: non-inlined calls and their inlined expansions compute the same defined values. The adjacent `mem::replace` change from `ptr::read`/`ptr::write` to `read_via_copy`/`write_via_move` is also only an implementation/Miri-diagnostic change for invalid aliasing, not a defined-result transformation. Therefore no source-grounded pair with identical inputs can produce different original/transformed defined values; manufacturing one would not correspond to the historical transformation.

analysis.originalLogic: The MIR inliner used a per-block top-down inline limit. For NormalInliner, `inline_limit_for_block` mapped the current inline history length to a limit: `0 => Some(usize::MAX), 1..=TOP_DOWN_DEPTH_LIMIT => Some(1), _ => None`. `process_blocks` then stopped processing the remaining newly-inlined blocks after one successful inline at depths 1..=5, and skipped further processing entirely beyond depth 5. A separate `add_function_level_costs` counted call-like terminators in a callee and added `CALL_PENALTY` when there was exactly one, using a local `is_call_like(bbd)` helper.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was not a wrong value rewrite but a missed inlining decision: when a trivial callee was reached only after prior top-down inlining, the old per-block limit could prevent it from being inlined at all. At history lengths 1..=5 the pass stopped after the first inline in that block range, and beyond depth 5 `inline_limit_for_block` returned `None` so newly exposed calls were not processed. Consequently calls to tiny single-basic-block callees such as `<usize as Step>::forward_unchecked` and `<f32 as PartialOrd>::le` remained as calls even though they are cheap and profitable to inline. The PR replaces the per-block limit with depth-aware eligibility: single-basic-block callees may still inline past the depth limit, unmarked `InlineAttr::None` callees are rejected past the limit, multi-block callees are rejected past the limit, and only multi-call expansions increment `top_down_counter`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR during the `Inline` pass, particularly call sites discovered inside blocks produced by a previous successful inline. Relevant callee shapes are: single-basic-block trivial methods (comparisons, `Step` operations, forwarding shims), multi-basic-block bodies, callees with `InlineAttr::None` versus marked `#[inline]`, and callees whose expansion introduces zero, one, or multiple call-like terminators. Representative induced programs are integer/slice range loops and diverging callback chains where `forward_unchecked`, `PartialOrd::le`, or `Fn::call` shims are exposed only after earlier inlining.
analysis.summary: The `Inline` MIR pass previously applied a per-block top-down limit: at depth 1..=5 it stopped after one successful inline in a block range, and beyond depth 5 it stopped processing new blocks entirely. That left trivial single-basic-block callees such as `<usize as Step>::forward_unchecked` and `<PartialOrd for f32>::le` as calls when they were found only after earlier inlining. This optimization PR replaces the per-block limit with a history depth limit plus a `top_down_counter` that counts multi-call expansions, while still allowing single-block callees past the limit when they are not `InlineAttr::None`. Updated MIR tests show the extra inlined scopes and `AddUnchecked`, and a new codegen test checks the resulting loop without LLVM optimization.
analysis.trigger: A call-like terminator appears in blocks newly created by a prior inline, or the inline history has grown past the old top-down depth. Under the old code, `inline_limit_for_block` returned `Some(1)` for history lengths 1..=5 and `None` thereafter, so a second call in the same block range and all calls beyond depth 5 were not considered for inlining. This is especially visible when a cheap single-basic-block callee such as `Step::forward_unchecked` or `PartialOrd::le` is exposed only after inlining a caller several levels deep.
preconditions: The program is compiled with MIR inlining enabled and the `Inline` pass runs on the caller.
The callsite is reached while processing blocks produced by an earlier successful inline, or the history length is already beyond the top-down depth.
The callee is a single-basic-block body for the new past-depth-limit allowance to apply; multi-block callees are rejected once past the limit.
The callee's codegen attributes are available: `InlineAttr::None` callees are rejected past the depth limit, while marked callees remain eligible.
`ForceInline` is a separate path: its `check_codegen_attributes_extra` always returns `Ok(())`, so it is not restricted by the normal inliner's depth check.
pitfalls: Do not equate 'single basic block' with 'single MIR statement': the eligibility check is `callee_body.basic_blocks.len() > 1`, and the block can still contain multiple statements and call-like terminators.

Do not assume every past-depth-limit inline is allowed: `NormalInliner::check_codegen_attributes_extra` rejects `InlineAttr::None` callees when `past_depth_limit()` is true, so `#[inline]`-marked versus unmarked callees can behave differently.
The depth guard uses strict `>` comparisons: `history.len() > HISTORY_DEPTH_LIMIT || top_down_counter > TOP_DOWN_DEPTH_LIMIT`; using `>=` changes the boundary behavior.

`top_down_counter` increments only when a successful inline introduces more than one call-like terminator (`new_calls_count > 1`), so a large number of trivial single-call/single-block inlines is not throttled by that counter.
The counter is reset only when the inline history becomes empty after processing, so it is scoped to one top-level inlining tree rather than globally across the caller.

Removing `inline_limit_for_block` also touched the shared `Inliner` trait used by `ForceInline`; forcing inlining must remain unrestricted and must not accidentally inherit the normal inliner's depth checks.
`check_codegen_attributes_extra` is part of the attribute gate, not an optional profitability hint; skipping it can allow an ineligible callee past the depth limit.

The `mem::replace` change to `read_via_copy`/`write_via_move` is an adjacent library change that removes `ptr::read`/`ptr::write` inline scopes and changes Miri stderr; do not treat those expectation updates as evidence about the inliner's own semantics.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-dump or mir-opt tests on a caller where a trivial single-basic-block callee is reachable only after several layers of inlining. Assert that the callee now appears as an inlined scope (for example `scope 8 (inlined <usize as Step>::forward_unchecked) {` and a `PartialOrd` inlined scope) and that the residual call disappears (for example `_12 = AddUnchecked(copy _11, const 1_usize);`). Include both marked/unmarked callees and single-block/multi-block callees to exercise the `InlineAttr::None` and `basic_blocks.len() > 1` past-depth checks separately. Use `tests/mir-opt/inline/exponential_runtime.rs`-style `// CHECK-NOT: inlined` assertions between expected nested inlines to verify the multi-call growth guard. Add a codegen test like `tests/codegen/range-loop.rs` with `-Copt-level=3 -C no-prepopulate-passes` and `// CHECK-NOT: define` to verify MIR cleanup produces a simple loop without relying on LLVM. Also retain an unconditional inline case for `ForceInline` to ensure its path remains unrestricted. Do not claim execution or reproduction; these are source/patch-derived test expectations only.
